motion.purpose: Delay before a wall card's first change so cards never flip in unison.

motion.name: public-card-hover
motion.purpose: Card lift and label rise (translateY 12px to 0, opacity 0 to 1).

motion.name: public-viewer

motion.name: public-filter
motion.value: 300ms colour; wall fade-in 500ms on filter change

motion.name: public-cover-zoom
motion.purpose: Blog cover hover zoom: 1.02 on leads, 1.03 on entries and Read next.

motion.name: public-reading-progress
motion.value: transform: scaleX(progress), origin left, rAF on scroll

breakpoints.name: lg

scopes.name: admin
exceptions: Live-preview frames in components/admin/project-editor.tsx and components/admin/testimonial-editor.tsx render public components; judge their contents against the public scope (The Preview Exception Rule).
The article editor canvas in components/admin/blog/rich-editor.tsx renders the public article-body rules on #111111; judge its contents against the public scope (The Preview Exception Rule).

narrative.northStar: The Studio Wall (admin) / The Gallery That Keeps Moving (public)
narrative.overview:
Admin world.

The admin looks like the work. The owner is a graphic designer, so the screen leads with large project images and client faces, and everything waiting for a reply is pinned above them. It turns down the usual back-office layout of KPI tiles over data tables. Lists exist (leads, job applications), but they are calm single panels with status pills. The full message and its actions sit on a detail page.

The material is the Xelvo brand at night: a near-black ground, slightly lifted panels separated by 1px white hairlines, warm off-white ink and one hot orange used sparingly. Depth comes from tone steps and hairlines, never from glow. Type is Plus Jakarta Sans in sentence case at bold weights with tight tracking, and every label uses plain English the owner would say out loud.

The signature is the live website preview. In the project and testimonial editors, a copy of the public site's card updates as the owner types or picks an image, so they see the website result before saving.

The article editor follows the same idea. The owner writes on the public article's own dark page and reading column, so what they type is what readers will see.

Public world.

The public site is a near-black gallery where the work leads. On the Portfolio page, a stage plays the studio's chosen projects one at a time, each shown whole, and below it a wall shows every project at its true shape. Multi-image projects page through their own images on staggered clocks, and any project opens into a quiet, opaque viewer with its story.

The material is charcoal (#111111) with a deeper black (#0b0b0b) behind images, white ink with translucent-white secondary text, full-colour images in 16px corners with a faint white hairline, and the brand's amber-to-orange gradient kept to a few marked places. Capsules and controls are solid dark fills, never glass. Plus Jakarta Sans carries everything, bold for headings.

The blog reads like the studio's journal. The newest article opens large, and the rest follow as calm entries in one column. A thin hairline, the journal spine, runs down the left of the feed with each entry's date on it. On the article page the same spine becomes the gradient reading-progress bar and the contents rail's active marker.
keyCharacteristics: Image-first: projects show as 14px-cornered photo tiles, not table rows.
One accent with a strict job list (primary action, needs-reply, logo).
Tonal layering on near-black with 1px white hairlines.
Sentence-case Plus Jakarta Sans, bold, tightly tracked headings, tabular numerals.
Plain-English status vocabulary with one hue per meaning.
Desktop sidebar, mobile top bar plus bottom tab bar.
A full-page article editor that writes on the public reading column.
The work leads: images at their own shape, full colour, nothing laid over them except a legibility scrim.
The brand gradient appears on the heading word, the active filter chip, the reading-progress bar and the contents marker, and the CTA gradient on CTAs; nowhere decorative.
Pill dots show position: the active dot stretches and turns orange.
Solid dark capsules and controls, no backdrop blur.
Category is quiet metadata under the title, never an eyebrow above it.
Motion runs only while on screen, pauses on hover, and stops under reduced motion.
Articles read at 18px on a 68ch measure, with the journal spine tying the feed and the article together.

rules.name: The Orange Reserve Rule
rules.body: Xelvo Orange means "do this" or "someone is waiting". It goes on primary actions, needs-reply state (badges, new dots, the New pill) and the logo, and on nothing else. Avatars are neutral charcoal. If orange marks something that is neither an action nor a waiting person, it is wrong. The keyboard focus ring is the one global exception (2px orange outline, 2px offset), because the build sets it in the scope stylesheet for accessibility. The article editor's caret, gap cursor and selected-block outline (2px, 3px offset) are the same focus device.

rules.name: The Preview Exception Rule
rules.body: Inside a live-preview frame, the public site's styling wins: the real public PortfolioCard on its #111111 ground in the project editor, the gradient avatar on the #121212 review card in the testimonial editor, and the article editor's writing canvas (Charcoal Ground with the public article body rules, including Link Orange links and list markers). A preview has to be the public card. That styling never leaves the frame.

rules.name: The Tint, Not Block Rule
rules.body: Status hues appear as a 12% tint with full-strength text plus a 6px dot. Solid fills are reserved for the orange count badge and the active filter tab.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, button and heading is sentence case. No uppercase tracked labels, and no kicker or eyebrow line above a heading. The date above the Home greeting is content, not a label.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: Statuses read New, Contacted, Interested, Won, Closed (leads), New, Reviewing, Contacted, Hired, Not selected (applications) and Draft, Scheduled, Published (articles). Navigation reads Home, Leads, Job applications, Projects, Testimonials, Blog. On mobile these shorten to Jobs and Reviews. No themed jargon.

rules.name: The First Card Leads Rule
rules.body: On the Home wall the first tile is the hero (2 columns by 2 rows once 3 or more show), and the tile count always fills the grid: 1, 2, 3 or 5. Never span every featured project. The client marks all of them featured, and spanning each one turns the wall into a stack of equal heroes.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons are flat orange with no coloured halo at rest or on hover. A coloured ring appears only as a focus state. This rule is admin-only (`.xa`).

rules.name: The Scrim Only Rule
rules.body: The only gradient in the admin's own chrome is the black legibility scrim at the bottom of project tiles (black 92% to transparent over the lower three quarters). Decorative gradients do not exist outside the preview frame.

rules.name: The Gradient Places Rule
rules.body: The brand gradient has exactly four jobs: the GradientText heading word, the active filter chip (and the blog's active category tab), the article's reading-progress bar and the contents rail's active marker. The CTA gradient has one: public call-to-action buttons. Neither is a background, a border or a decoration. The journal spine's hairline is a neutral white fade (22% to 5%), not the brand gradient.

rules.name: The Glow Belongs Outside Rule
rules.body: The orange glow on public CTA buttons is a public-world device. The admin's No Glow Rule stays in force inside `.xa`, and the glow never enters the admin's own chrome.

rules.name: The Metadata Below Rule
rules.body: A project's category always sits under its title as muted metadata (white at 70%, medium weight). It never sits above the title as a kicker or eyebrow. Blog entries follow the same rule: category, reading time and date sit in one meta line under the excerpt.

rules.name: The Reading Column Rule
rules.body: Article text is 18px with 1.75 leading on a 68ch measure, set by one shared article-body stylesheet. The public article page and the admin editor canvas both use it, so the owner writes exactly what readers see. Never restyle article text in only one of the two.

rules.name: The True Shape Rule
rules.body: The wall shows each project at its cover's real proportions in masonry columns. A multi-image card takes its height from the cover, and later images crop to that cover's shape. Never force the wall into equal cropped cells.

rules.name: The Admin Categories Rule
rules.body: Filter chips are built from the categories the owner types in the admin, exactly as typed (trimmed, grouped case-insensitively, shown with the first spelling and a count), after an "All" chip. No invented taxonomy.

rules.name: The One Portfolio Route Rule
rules.body: `/portfolio` is the portfolio. `/projects` permanently redirects (308) to it.

rules.name: The Journal Spine Rule
rules.body: The spine is one system used in exactly three places: the feed's 1px hairline (white 22% fading to 5%) with a 13px dateline and a 9px hollow node (Charcoal Ground with a white-30% ring) level with each cover's top, on lg only; the article's 3px brand-gradient reading-progress bar, pinned to the bottom edge of the fixed Header; and the contents rail, which repeats the same hairline with a 2px brand-gradient marker on the section being read. Do not add it anywhere else.

rules.name: The Legibility Scrim Rule
rules.body: The only gradient laid over an image is a bottom legibility scrim: on cards, black 85% to 40% at 55% to transparent; on the stage caption, #0b0b0b at 92% to 60% at 60% to transparent. It exists so text can be read, never for mood.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: Public capsules and controls are solid dark fills: the dot capsule is #0b0b0b at 75%, the Header is #0b0b0b at 95%, and the preview backdrop is opaque. No backdrop blur.

dos: Do keep Xelvo Orange to primary actions, needs-reply state (badges, new dots, the New pill) and the logo.
Do show projects as image tiles with 14px corners, and let the first card lead the Home wall in a grid of 1, 2, 3 or 5 tiles with no empty cells.
Do show status as a tinted pill with a dot, using the plain-English vocabulary: New, Contacted, Interested, Won, Closed / New, Reviewing, Contacted, Hired, Not selected.
Do separate surfaces with tone steps and 1px white hairlines (8%, or 14% for controls).
Do confirm every delete and every unsaved-changes discard in an in-app dialog, and toast every save.
Do mirror the public card exactly inside a live preview, including its gradients, by rendering the real public component.
Do show article status as Draft, Scheduled or Published pills, and write articles on the shared article-body canvas.
Do set public pages on Charcoal Ground (#111111) with Deep Black (#0b0b0b) behind images.
Do frame images in 16px corners with a 1px white-8% ring, and show the wall at each cover's true shape.
Do show the stage and preview images contained, never cropped.
Do keep the brand gradient to the GradientText heading word and the active filter chip, and the CTA gradient with its glow to public CTAs.
Do mark position with pill dots: the active dot stretched and orange, every hit area at least 24px.
Do put the category under the title as muted metadata.
Do run auto-advance only while on screen (35% visible), pause it on hover and in hidden tabs, stop it under reduced motion, and restart the full interval after a manual pick.
Do build filter chips from the admin's categories exactly as typed.
Do keep the Home case-study cards in their original white design; only their image area plays and opens the preview.
Do set article text at 18px with 1.75 leading on a 68ch measure, from the shared article-body rules.
Do keep the journal spine to the feed's dateline hairline, the reading-progress bar and the contents marker.
donts: Don't put a coloured glow or halo on buttons or cards; primary buttons are flat.
Don't make avatars orange or use the brand gradient anywhere outside the preview frame.
Don't add kicker or eyebrow labels, uppercase tracked labels, or themed jargon names for statuses and sections.
Don't span every featured project on the Home wall, or leave an empty grid cell.
Don't build a KPI tile row over a data table as the Home view.
Don't use Ash (faint) for text the owner has to read.
Don't use backdrop blur or glass panels on public capsules and controls; use solid dark fills.
Don't lay any gradient over an image except the bottom legibility scrim.
Don't put the category above a title as an eyebrow.
Don't crop the stage or preview image, or force the wall into equal cropped cells.
Don't replace the Home case-study cards with portfolio cards.
Don't carry the public CTA glow or brand gradient into the admin's own chrome.
Don't paint the spine hairline itself with the brand gradient; it is a neutral white fade.
